claim: Of [6ii] She ran to the station / two miles, “adding a goal such as to the station or an extent adjunct such as two miles makes the clause bounded”.
evidence_summary: Under “Complement status of non-temporal extent elements”, §5.3 (p. 692) says: “While elements expressing extent in the temporal domain (duration) are generally adjuncts, those in the spatial and scalar change domains have the properties of complements.” It argues this from licensing by the verb (cycle) and do so anaphora, then speaks of “Extent complements”. Page 665 says “the term ‘adjunct’ covers modifiers in the VP or clause together with related supplements”, so the word can’t include complements.
finding: Ran is a motion verb like the cycle of §5.3’s licensing argument, so two miles is a complement by the chapter’s own criteria. The same slip occurs on p. 689 (CG-0128) and p. 706 (CG-0134).
proposed_wording: adding a goal such as to the station or an extent element such as two miles makes the clause bounded
inference: Is two miles in She ran two miles an adjunct?

evidence.passage: §1, p. 668. “or an extent adjunct such as two miles makes the clause bounded”.
evidence.example: Page 692, §5.3, “Complement status of non-temporal extent elements”.
evidence.establishes: The chapter treats spatial extent elements as complements.
